from solution import concatenate_strings


def test_issue_example_three_names():
    """Pairwise concatenation of two string tuples as in example."""
    # "Manjeet"+" Singh"="Manjeet Singh", "Nikhil"+" Meherwal"="Nikhil Meherwal", "Akshat"+" Garg"="Akshat Garg"
    assert concatenate_strings(("Manjeet", "Nikhil", "Akshat"), (" Singh", " Meherwal", " Garg")) == ('Manjeet Singh', 'Nikhil Meherwal', 'Akshat Garg')


def test_issue_single_element():
    """Concatenation of two string tuples works for single-element tuples."""
    # "a"+"b"="ab"
    assert concatenate_strings(("a",), ("b",)) == ("ab",)


def test_issue_two_elements():
    """Concatenation of two string tuples joins each pair in order."""
    # "Hello"+"Foo"="HelloFoo", "World"+"Bar"="WorldBar"
    assert concatenate_strings(("Hello", "World"), ("Foo", "Bar")) == ("HelloFoo", "WorldBar")


def test_issue_both_empty():
    """Concatenation of two empty tuples is an empty tuple."""
    # no pairs to join, expected ()
    assert concatenate_strings((), ()) == ()


def test_issue_empty_strings():
    """Concatenation of empty strings yields empty strings."""
    # ""+""="", ""+""=""
    assert concatenate_strings(("", ""), ("", "")) == ("", "")


def test_issue_five_elements():
    """Concatenation of two string tuples works for five pairs."""
    # "a"+"1"="a1", "b"+"2"="b2", "c"+"3"="c3", "d"+"4"="d4", "e"+"5"="e5"
    assert concatenate_strings(("a", "b", "c", "d", "e"), ("1", "2", "3", "4", "5")) == ("a1", "b2", "c3", "d4", "e5")


def test_issue_numeric_strings():
    """Concatenation of numeric strings concatenates textually."""
    # "12"+"56"="1256", "34"+"78"="3478"
    assert concatenate_strings(("12", "34"), ("56", "78")) == ("1256", "3478")


def test_issue_unicode_strings():
    """Concatenation of two string tuples preserves unicode characters."""
    # "café"+" ☕"="café ☕", "naïve"+" ✨"="naïve ✨"
    assert concatenate_strings(("café", "naïve"), (" ☕", " ✨")) == ("café ☕", "naïve ✨")


def test_contract_returns_tuple():
    """Concatenation of two string tuples returns a tuple."""
    # "x"+"1"="x1", "y"+"2"="y2"; check type is tuple
    assert isinstance(concatenate_strings(("x", "y"), ("1", "2")), tuple)


def test_contract_does_not_modify_inputs():
    """Function must not mutate the input tuples."""
    tup1 = ("a", "b")
    tup2 = ("1", "2")
    concatenate_strings(tup1, tup2)
    assert (tup1, tup2) == (("a", "b"), ("1", "2"))


def test_contract_returns_new_object():
    """Function returns a new tuple object distinct from inputs."""
    tup1 = ("p", "q")
    tup2 = ("r", "s")
    # "p"+"r"="pr", "q"+"s"="qs"; result must not be either input object
    assert concatenate_strings(tup1, tup2) is not tup1 and concatenate_strings(tup1, tup2) is not tup2
